title: Waqf and ibtida' in Ya-Sin 25 to 32: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y10 lesson 20 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Waqf and ibtida' in Ya-Sin 25 to 32 rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 20. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

arabic.text: ۞ وَمَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ مِن جُندٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا كُنَّا مُنزِلِينَ (٢٨)

head: Not this
This
rows: Stopping at «وَمَآ أَنزَلْنَا» (36:28) and moving on
That stop is qabih (it reads as 'We did not send down'); go back and continue to complete the meaning

keywords.def: stopping on a word, with a breath
a bad stop that changes the meaning

questions.q: If you must breathe in 36:28, where is the best place, and where do you restart?
questions.a: After «مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ», restarting at «وَمَا كُنَّا مُنزِلِينَ»; never after «وَمَآ أَنزَلْنَا».

questions.q: Stop map (pupil PDF): mark every sign and safe breath point in 36:25 to 32. Today's rota group recites 36:25 to 32.
questions.a: Signs at 36:26 and 36:30 marked; safe points before «وَمَا كُنَّا» (36:28).

questions.q: Extend: label the end of 36:27 tamm, kafi or hasan.
questions.a: Tamm: the man's speech ends; 36:28 starts a new idea.

questions.q: Stretch: why is stopping in the middle of a long ayah only for need?
questions.a: The ayah end is the sunnah stop; inside, only stop for breath at a sound place.
A) continuing is better. ۖ (صلى): continuing is better, stopping allowed.

questions.q: Think again: 36:30 has a waqf sign in the middle. How does a pause there help the listener?
questions.a: It separates the cry of regret from its reason: every messenger was mocked.
